scorecards.inningsCommentary: India embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 287 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. Rohit Sharma anchored the innings with a resolute 47, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. South Africa's bowling response was spearheaded by L Ngidi (6/39), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 151/10 (50.2 ov), India succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as South Africa's bowlers closed out the victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at SuperSport Park commenced with high tactical intensity as South Africa posted 335/10 (113.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 307/10 (92.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: L Ngidi (6/39), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Virat Kohli delivered a masterclass for India (158 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (South Africa 47%) and allowing South Africa to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, India faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. South Africa's bowling unit, bolstered by R Ashwin (41 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing South Africa won by 135 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: South Africa's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While India produced fighting phases, South Africa won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
